newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer buys rights to sell aspirin in France.
newsitem.headline: Bayer buys rights to sell aspirin in France.

text.p: German Bayer AG, creater of aspirin, one of the world's best-known painkillers, said on Friday it had bought the rights to sell the product in France, where the name is not a registered trademark.
The drugs and chemicals group purchased the licence to sell Aspirine du Rhone from French drugs group Rhone Poulenc Rorer for an undisclosed sum.
Aspirin was first synthesised 100 years ago by Bayer chemist Felix Hoffmann and has become one of the group's best selling products generating some 850 million marks in sales per year.
While Aspirin is a registered trademark in more than 70 nations, including the U.S. and Germany, it does not have trademark protection in France and Britain.
In France the product is currently the third best-selling over-the-counter medication.

In 1994 Bayer spent one billion U.S. dollars to buy back its famous trademark and the rights to use the brandname Bayer in the United States by purchasing Sterling Winthrop's self-medication business.
